note: THE ONE PAYLOAD BOTH SUITES PARSE for the backlog autoscaler's durable bead claim. `beadIds` are ids the Sparkle board really carries and hands to `acquireBeadClaim`; `claimantIds` are what apps/desktop/src/services/autoscalerClaim.ts's mintAutoscalerClaimantId ACTUALLY produces. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/autoscaler_claim.rs feeds every one of these to the REAL is_bead_id / is_actor_id validators, and the TS half pins the mint's OUTPUT to the same shape. Neither side may be edited alone. This exists because the sibling lease shipped a mint whose ':' and '#' its own Rust validator rejected — 49,381 sweeps, zero dispatches, not one log line naming the cause (sparkle-2hsrlz). A claim that is silently always `invalid` is a spawner with NO de-duplication at all.

beadIds.why: The ordinary shape the board carries.
A DOTTED CHILD bead. The autoscaler works an epic's children, so this is the common case, not an edge one — and '.' is exactly the character an agent-id validator would have rejected.

rejectedBeadIds.why: Empty is not an id, and an empty store key would collide with anything.
A slash would let a hand-edited store forge a path-shaped key.
Whitespace: a key that round-trips differently than it was typed.
Only dots — no alphanumeric at all, which is path-ish nonsense rather than a bead.

claimantIds.why: The exact production shape mintAutoscalerClaimantId produces: a fixed prefix and 16 lowercase hex characters. No repo slug, no timestamp with a colon, nothing user-controlled — the sibling lease's mint took a repo slug and that is what made it forgeable into an invalid id.
All-zero randomness is a legal draw and must still be accepted.
